issues.details: Batch 5 apply review: the bridge URL-decodes GET query values twice, so a literal =, &, % or + in a value is cut short or rewritten (get_function_labels for the readable name std::_RefCountedPtr<...>::operator= answers 'Function not found: ...::operator'; search_functions name_pattern=operator= searches for 'operator'). Encoding the value twice (%253D on the wire) reads it exactly. GhidraBridge.request encodes once; the receipt's name-keyed get_struct_layout/get_enum_values reads therefore mark the two live types whose names contain & (Metrowerks alloc_ptr<...&...> and details::compressed_pair_imp<...&...>) as unreadable-name, failing closed rather than misreading. Writes use JSON POST bodies and are unaffected; functions and globals are read by address. Fixing the encoding (double-encode GET values, after confirming every GET endpoint the tools use double-decodes) makes those types readable and so changes the receipt of any accepted scope that contains them (e.g. the type foundation); it needs a receipt-schema or rebaseline plan so restore-accepted replays still reproduce. Documented under GHIDRA.md Bridge hazards.
issues.summary: Bridge GET values are decoded twice; =, &, % and + in names are misread

issues.details: Batch 35 (apply accepted at tracker revision 253). libpttclient.cpp g_buffer (0x5630c0, .symtab 8192 bytes) and g_buffer_hb (0x5650c0, 32768 bytes) are DWARF arrays of fundamental 0xA510 (u_long128), rendered uint16[512] and uint16[2048]; Ghidra's builtin /uint16 is 16 bytes. GhidraMCP 6.0.0 apply_data_type resolves names through ServiceUtils.resolveWellKnownType first (uint16 -> UnsignedShortDataType, 2 bytes), so the first batch 35 apply wrote ushort[512]/ushort[2048]; read-back caught it, the unsaved program was closed without saving, and tools 4044fb7/49edd7a now skip global types whose base name is in that table. Both globals have no data item.
